Find the $x$-coordinates of the points where the circle $(x-4)^{2}+(y+1)^{2}=10$ intersects the line $y=x-3$ (sketched above).
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points, we substitute $y=x-3$ into the equation of the circle and solve the resulting equation for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2}+(y+1)^{2} & =10 \\ (x-4)^{2}+(x-3+1)^{2} & =10 \\ (x-4)^{2}+(x-2)^{2} & =10 \\ {x}^{2}-8x+16+{x}^{2}-4x+4 & =10 \\ 2{x}^{2}-12x+10 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-6x+5 & =0 \\ (x-1)(x-5) & =0 \\ x & =1,5.\end{aligned}
$$
